title: Problem Evidence Packet
description: Input to the Problem Evidence Auditor. Raw observations (evidence), interpretations, and product claims are kept in separate top-level collections and MUST NOT be merged. This schema owns STRUCTURE only; requirement definitions live in checklist.json and policy semantics live in SPEC.md.

packetVersion.description: Version of this packet's contents, incremented when evidence is added or corrected.

packetPurpose.description: 'fixture' = benchmark packet used to exercise the auditor; synthetic evidence MAY contribute toward pass. 'audit' = real evaluation; synthetic evidence MUST NOT contribute toward pass. See SPEC.md Policy 2.

notes.description: Free-text context about the packet as a whole. Never treated as evidence.

text.description: The segment exactly as the team states it. Recorded verbatim, including vagueness.

attributes.description: Structured segment boundaries, where the team has committed to them. Absence of an attribute is a signal for the REQ-1 definition check, not a schema error.

problemHypothesis.description: The problem the team believes exists. Context for the auditor; never itself evidence.

claims.description: The propositions to be audited. Claims are supplied, never extracted by the auditor from prose.

claimScope.description: Determines the evidence sufficiency rule applied. See SPEC.md 'Claim scope and sufficiency'.

definedThreshold.description: The quantitative or qualitative bar the claim commits to. Required for a fail verdict: counterevidence must falsify the claim AT this threshold. Null means no threshold was stated.

evidence.description: Raw records only. Each record holds what was observed or reported, NOT what it is thought to mean. May be empty; an empty array is a valid packet and produces not-testable findings.

interpretations.description: Human readings of the evidence. Kept strictly separate from evidence. The auditor MAY report an interpretation but MUST NOT cite it as support for a status.

inferenceType.description: 'causal-claim', 'prediction' and 'speculation' are flagged by the auditor as unsupported-by-construction unless separately evidenced.

evidenceRecord.description: One evidence record. The dimensions below are DESCRIPTIVE FACTS about how the record came to exist, deliberately kept as separate axes. There is no single linear evidence ranking; the auditor combines axes per requirement. See SPEC.md 'Evidence model'.

evidenceCategory.description: What kind of thing this record is. Category is not a grade.

proximity.description: How far the record sits from the behavior it describes. Independent of category and of fit.

origin.description: 'field' = collected from the real world. 'synthetic' = invented. Governs whether the record may contribute toward pass in an 'audit' packet.

synthetic.description: MUST equal (origin == 'synthetic'). Retained as an explicit, hard-to-miss boolean.

sourceId.description: Pseudonymous participant/organization id. Two records sharing a sourceId are NOT independent.

independence.description: 'related' = reached via another participant (referral chain, same employer, same association).

content.description: What was actually recorded. No interpretation, no conclusions, no adjectives supplied by the packet author.

observation.description: The record itself: quoted words, described artifact contents, or observation notes.

scope.description: Coverage of the record: who and how long. Determines whether prevalence and segment-wide claims can be reached at all.

segmentFit.description: Assessed against product.statedTargetSegment. 'unknown' when the packet does not record enough to tell.

declaredRelevance.description: Requirements the packet author believes this record speaks to. An author pointer only: the auditor derives its own requirement-fit and MUST NOT defer to this field.

limitations.description: Known defects of this record: recall bias, leading question, self-selection, single site, partial timeframe, missing provenance. Required; use an empty array only when genuinely none are known.

supersession.description: Explicit, author-supplied replacement relationships. Source identity or chronology alone never implies supersession. Every condition is recorded so the auditor can verify it against SPEC.md OPEN-04.

replacementStatement.description: How this record explicitly corrects, replaces, or invalidates the older record.

provenanceComparison.description: The newer record must have equal or stronger provenance.
